guard: none
why: Verified directly: src/index.ts's handleAddNode validates only projectPath/scenePath (validatePath) and nodeType (validateClassName), but forwards args.properties verbatim (line 1626-1627) with no inspection. In godot_operations.gd (read in full, lines 500-528), any string property value beginning with 'res://' is passed straight to load() and then applied via new_node.set(property, value). Every Godot Node has a settable 'script' property, so a caller can supply {"properties":{"script":"res://payload.gd"}} to attach an arbitrary GDScript to the node; the scene is then packed and saved to disk, and since add_child (called right after) triggers _ready() on the node, the attached script's code executes inside the running Godot process. Notably, a sibling function get_script_by_name explicitly documents (lines 91-94) that raw res:// paths are intentionally rejected there 'to prevent arbitrary script instantiation from agent-supplied input' — proving the maintainers recognize this exact risk, yet the add_node properties path has no equivalent guard.
